title: Serum thymosin β4 levels in patients with hepatitis B virusrelated liver failure

what_it_measured.text: Serum thymosin β4 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and Child-Pugh and model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) scores were calculated for each patient on admission.
Abstract AIM: To investigate whether serum thymosin β4 can provide diagnostic or prognostic information in liver failure patients caused by chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection.

endpoint.text: Serum thymosin β4 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and Child-Pugh and model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) scores were calculated for each patient on admission.

METHODS: Serum thymosin β4 levels were measured in 30 patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), 31 patients with chronic liver failure (CLF), 30 patients with compensated liver cirrhosis (CR) and 32 patients with chronic hepatitis B and 30 healthy controls.

reported_results.text: In patients with chronic liver disease, there was a positive relationship between thymosin β4 levels and albumin, choline esterase, and platelet (P < 0.001), and negative relationship with alanine aminotransferase (P = 0.020), aspartate aminotransferase, total bilirubin, international normalized ratio of prothrombin time, and Child-Pugh and MELD scores (P < 0.001).
The levels of thymosin β4 in liver failure (ACLF or CLF) patients were markedly lower than that in CR (P < 0.001), and a difference was also found between CLF and ACLF patients (P = 0.038).

Serum thymosin β4 levels in patients with hepatitis B virusrelated liver failure Tao Han, Ying Liu, Huan Liu, Zheng-Yan Zhu, Yan Li, Shi-Xiang Xiao, Zhen Guo, Zhen-Gang Zhao RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, serum thymosin β4 levels in ACLF, CLF, CR and chronic hepatitis B patients were significantly lower, 6.5047 (4.7879-10.5314) μg/mL vs 0.4632 (0.2759-0.8768) μg/mL, 0.6981 (0.5209-1.2008) μg/mL, 1.8053 (0.8110-2.3397) μg/mL, 3.7803 (1.8570-6.4722) μg/mL, respectively (P < 0.001).
The thymosin β4 in ACLF and CLF patients was markedly reduced as compared with that in CR patients (P < 0.001).
The median thymosin β4 concentrations of non-survivors were significantly lower than those of survivors (P < 0.001, Table 4).
